title: Token residency shard controller and GPU slab optimization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's token KV cache suffers from long-tail fragmentation on multi-tenant GPUs when mixed sequence-length workloads interleave. Current slab placement policies favour first-fit allocations which leaves many micro-holes and forces background compaction that spikes latency and increases GPU memory overhead. Continuous batching increases pressure on KV residency and amplifies fragmentation over time.

Goal:
Design and implement a Token Residency Shard Controller (TRSC) that orchestrates fine-grained placement and proactive coalescence of token slots across GPU slabs to reduce fragmentation, lower background compaction frequency, and improve steady-state memory utilization without regressing p50/p99 latency. This work complements ongoing KV compaction heuristics but focuses on allocation-time decisions and lightweight online rehoming of slots.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Introduce 'residency windows' per slab: short-lived metadata buckets tracking token lifetime distribution and access heat.
- Allocate new tokens into residency-aware shards (hot/mid/cold) to colocate similar-lifetime entries and reduce churn.
- Implement a lightweight Shard Controller that schedules opportunistic micro-coalescence passes at safe points (between micro-batches) rather than heavyweight global compactions.
- Add slot skyline telemetry: fragmentation ratio, average hole width, coalescence efficiency, and compaction-trigger rate.
- Integrate with continuous batching: controller exposes soft-placement hints to the batcher to favour batch-local allocations on underutilized slabs.

Design details / trade-offs:
- Proactive micro-coalescence vs. background compaction: micro-coalescence must be cheap (<0.5ms per slab on average) to avoid interfering with p50. We'll prioritize in-place merges and pointer remapping where possible.
- Strict locality increases packing but risks hotspotting GPU SM resources; controller will rate-limit writes to slabs flagged as hot.
- Residency window duration is workload-dependent. We'll start with conservative defaults (1-2 minutes) and expose tuning via runtime flags and Optimize recommendations.
- Avoid full data migration during initial rollout: first phase will implement metadata-only placement and shallow swaps; deeper relocation is gated behind telemetry thresholds.

Telemetry & KPI targets:
- Reduce fragmentation ratio (holes / allocated) by >=35% on mixed-length production traces.
- Decrease frequency of full-slab compactions by >=50% over 24h windows.
- No more than 5% regression on p99 generation latency during steady-state.
- Memory headroom improvement equivalent to recovering 6-8% GPU RAM on average for inference fleets.

Implementation tasks (tentative):
1) Data model changes: add per-slab residency window structures and shard assignment metadata (low-overhead).
2) Allocator changes: residency-aware allocator path with shard hints and soft placement.
3) Shard Controller: scheduling loop for micro-coalescence, rate limiting, safety checks.
4) Batcher integration: placement hints API and simple backpressure hook.
5) Telemetry: Prometheus metrics + Console dashboard for fragmentation skyline and compaction events.
6) Experiments: perf harness run against production-like trace (see artifacts).
7) Rollout: canary on dedicated pool -> gradual ramp with automatic rollback on regressions.

Artifacts / references:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Token+Residency+Shard+Controller+Spec (internal)
- Perf benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/tree/main/benchmarks/kv-frag
- Initial PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7821
- Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-fragmentation/triage

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for residency metadata and allocator path merged.
- Micro-coalescence loop implemented and feature-flagged.
- Telemetry emitted and dashboard showing expected signals on staged traces.
- End-to-end canary demonstrating >=20% fragmentation reduction on mixed-length trace without >5% p99 regression.
- Rollout runbook and automatic rollback guard in place.

Rollout plan:
Phase A (feature-flagged internal canary): 1-2 dedicated GPUs with synthetic mixed-length traffic. Monitor fragmentation metrics and latencies for 48h.
Phase B (customer-safe canary): route 5% of live traffic for customers on Dedicated. Observe for 7 days.
Phase C (ramp): 25% -> 75% -> 100% over weeks, with thresholds for rollback if p99 regresses or compaction events spike.

Rollback/mitigation:
- Feature flag off (immediate); Shard Controller idempotently reverts placement hints.
- Emergency path: fall back to existing compaction heuristic by toggling runtime knob.

Security and compliance notes:
- No customer data changes; controller operates on token residency metadata only. No additional encryption or KMS integration required.

Documentation and SDK notes:
- Update runtime docs: allocation tuning knobs and Optimize recommendations.
- Console: add fragmentation chart and incident playbook link.

Expected follow-ups:
- Phase 2: deeper relocation with copy-on-write moves for high-gain slabs.
- Phase 3: cross-GPU cooperative rehoming for Dedicated clusters when hot/cold imbalance persists.
